business_news.title: Oil prices jump as Trump rejects Iran's response to US peace plan
business_news.summary:
STORY: Oil prices rallied Monday, a day after President Donald Trump said Iran's response to a U.S. peace proposal was "unacceptable."

By early afternoon in Asia, international benchmark Brent crude futures were up around 4% at $105 a barrel, with U.S. oil seeing similar gains. 

That reversed declines seen last week, when prices had fallen on hopes of a peace agreement. 

On Monday, the signs of a fraying ceasefire raised supply fears as the Strait of Hormuz stayed largely closed.

It's normally the route for around a fifth of global oil and gas shipments. 

Iran on Sunday released a response to the proposal focused on ending the war.

According to Iranian state TV, Tehran also included a demand for compensation for war damages and emphasized its sovereignty over the Strait of Hormuz.

Analysts say the market's attention now shifts to Trump's visit to China.

The president is scheduled to arrive in Beijing on Wednesday and U.S. officials say he's expected to discuss Iran and other topics with Chinese leader Xi Jinping.
